request: My statement is full of things like 'AMZN Mktp DE' and 'PP.4711.PP'. Which shops did I really pay the most at this year? Use the readable names.

plan.title: The shops I paid the most
plan.question: The eight merchants with the highest spending in 2025, named by their enriched title rather than by the raw booking text, one row per merchant, ordered by the figure, columns merchant and total_eur.

sql:
SELECT coalesce(title, counterparty, description) AS merchant,
       ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE amount < 0 AND category IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY merchant
ORDER BY total_eur DESC
LIMIT 8
reasoning_plan:
the request is written in English, so language en
it ranks merchants against each other, one figure each
shop names are long, so horizontal bars read them without tilting
the columns are merchant and total_eur, the euro figure last
the period is the whole year the data covers
reasoning_code:
the shape is bar_horizontal, so the mark is barX
the columns are merchant and total_eur
the euros are on x and the names on y

request: Per month, what goes to AMZN Mktp DE against what goes to Kaufland and REWE?

plan.title: Amazon, Kaufland and REWE per month
plan.question: Spending per month of 2025 at Amazon marketplace, at Kaufland and at REWE, one row per month and shop, columns month as 'YYYY-MM', merchant and total_eur.

sql:
SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month,
       coalesce(title, counterparty, description) AS merchant,
       ROUND(-SUM(amount), 2) AS total_eur
FROM transaction_view
WHERE amount < 0
  AND (lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%amzn mktp%'
       OR lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%kaufland%'
       OR lower(description || ' ' || coalesce(counterparty, '')) LIKE '%rewe%')
GROUP BY month, merchant
ORDER BY month, merchant

three shops are followed over the months, so three series over one period

the columns are month, merchant and total_eur, the euro figure last

the columns are month, merchant and total_eur
the euro scale is built in a factory so the chart can call it

       CASE WHEN booked_on < '2025-12-01' THEN 'November' ELSE 'Dezember' END AS period,

GROUP BY topic, period
ORDER BY topic, period

request: How do my grocery costs pile up over the year?

plan.title: Groceries, piled up over the year
plan.question: The running total of spending in the category Groceries over the months of 2025, one row per month with the cumulative figure, columns month as 'YYYY-MM' and cumulative_eur.

sql:
WITH months AS (
  SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', booked_on) AS month, SUM(-amount) AS spent
  FROM transaction_view
  WHERE amount < 0 AND category = 'Groceries'
  GROUP BY month
)
SELECT month, ROUND(SUM(spent) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS cumulative_eur
FROM months
ORDER BY month
reasoning_plan:
the request is written in English, so language en
"pile up" is a running total over the months
an area under the running line shows how fast it grows
the columns are month and cumulative_eur
the period is the whole year
reasoning_code:
the shape is area, so areaY draws the band and lineY its edge
the columns are month and cumulative_eur
the euro scale is configured so it keeps its own settings
